questions.stem: Which of these is an overseas department and region of France?
questions.explanation: La Réunion, in the Indian Ocean, is part of France, along with Guadeloupe, Martinique, la Guyane and Mayotte. Madagascar, its neighbour, is an independent country where French is an official language.

questions.stem: Which French-governed territory lies closest to Australia?
questions.explanation: New Caledonia lies in the Pacific east of Queensland, and its capital is Nouméa. French Polynesia is also in the Pacific, but several thousand kilometres further east.

questions.stem: Which overseas region is home to the European space launch site at Kourou?
questions.explanation: French Guiana, on the north-east coast of South America, is close to the equator, which suits rocket launches. Martinique is an island in the Caribbean.

questions.stem: Tahiti is part of which French overseas collectivity?
questions.explanation: Tahiti is the main island of French Polynesia, and its capital is Papeete. New Caledonia is also in the Pacific, but much further west.

questions.stem: In which Canadian province is French the sole official language?
questions.explanation: Québec's Charter of the French Language makes French its only official language. New Brunswick is officially bilingual, with English and French both official.

questions.stem: In Belgium and Switzerland, what does « nonante » mean?
questions.explanation: Belgian and Swiss French use « septante » (70) and « nonante » (90) for France's « soixante-dix » and « quatre-vingt-dix ». Recognising them matters when reading or hearing prices and dates from those countries.

questions.stem: What does « le courriel », a word first promoted in Québec, mean?
questions.explanation: « Courriel » blends « courrier » and « électronique ». It was adopted officially in France as well, as an alternative to « e-mail ». A letterbox is « une boîte aux lettres ».

questions.stem: What is the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie?
options: The French ministry in charge of the overseas territories
The organisation that sets and marks the French bac
The academy that publishes the French dictionary
A body of countries sharing the French language
questions.explanation: The OIF brings together countries and governments where French is used, and promotes the language and cooperation. The dictionary belongs to the Académie française.

questions.stem: Why is French an official language in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and Benin?
options: French is their most widely spoken first language.
They are overseas departments of France.
They were French colonies until around 1960.
They were Belgian colonies until around 1960.
questions.explanation: These countries were part of French West Africa and became independent around 1960, keeping French in government and schools. Most people speak other languages first, such as Wolof in Senegal.

questions.stem: What is the motto of the French Republic?
questions.explanation: « Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité » comes from the Revolution and appears on public buildings. « Travail, Famille, Patrie » was the motto of the Vichy regime during the Second World War.

questions.stem: How long is the French president's term of office, « le quinquennat »?
questions.explanation: « Quinquennat » comes from the Latin for five years. Until 2002 the term was seven years, « le septennat », which is why that answer is tempting.

questions.stem: Which two chambers make up the French Parliament?
options: la Chambre des communes et le Sénat
le Conseil d'État et le Sénat
questions.explanation: Parliament has the Assemblée nationale, elected directly, and the Sénat, elected indirectly. L'Élysée is the president's palace, not a chamber.

questions.stem: Under the Fifth Republic, who appoints the Prime Minister?
options: The voters, in a separate election
questions.explanation: The president appoints the Prime Minister, who leads the government and answers to the Assemblée nationale. There is no separate popular vote for Prime Minister.

questions.stem: When was the Fifth Republic founded?
questions.explanation: Its constitution was adopted in 1958, when Charles de Gaulle returned to power. 1789 is the start of the Revolution, and 1968 the year of the May protests.

questions.stem: What is « la laïcité »?
options: The official religion of the state
A ban on all religious belief
questions.explanation: Under the law of 1905, the state recognises no religion and stays neutral, while individuals keep freedom of belief. It does not ban religion, which is the misconception behind 'a ban on all religious belief'.

questions.stem: Who is « Marianne »?
options: The female figure symbolising the Republic
A queen of France before the Revolution
Joan of Arc's name before she became a soldier
questions.explanation: Marianne personifies the Republic and appears on stamps, coins and busts in town halls. She is a symbol, not a historical person.

questions.stem: What does « le 14 juillet » commemorate?
options: The crowning of Napoléon as emperor
The storming of the Bastille in 1789
The armistice that ended the First World War
questions.explanation: The national holiday marks the storming of the Bastille, a symbol of royal power, at the start of the Revolution. The 1918 armistice is remembered on 11 November.

questions.stem: Under the Ancien Régime, who belonged to « le tiers état »?
options: The king's ministers, advisers and judges
questions.explanation: Society was divided into three estates: the clergy, the nobility, and the Third Estate, which was everyone else. That was the great majority, from peasants to wealthy merchants.

questions.stem: What was the « Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen » of 1789?
options: A statement of rights from the Revolution
The treaty that ended the Hundred Years' War
The law separating church and state
questions.explanation: Adopted in August 1789, it set out rights such as liberty and equality before the law. Napoléon's civil code came later, in 1804.

questions.stem: Which lasting reform is associated with Napoléon Bonaparte?
options: The Declaration of the Rights of Man
The abolition of the monarchy in 1792
questions.explanation: The Code civil, or Code Napoléon, organised French civil law and influenced legal systems across Europe and beyond. The Declaration of 1789 came before he held power.

questions.stem: Why is Jeanne d'Arc famous?
options: She led the crowd that stormed the Bastille in 1789.
She led a Resistance network in the Second World War.
She was the first woman elected to the Assemblée nationale.
She helped lift the siege of Orléans in the Hundred Years' War.
questions.explanation: In 1429 Joan of Arc helped lift the English siege of Orléans, and Charles VII was then crowned. She lived some 350 years before the Revolution.

questions.stem: What was « l'Appel du 18 juin » 1940?
options: Pétain's speech asking the French to accept the new regime
The Allied call to the French to prepare for the D-Day landings
De Gaulle's broadcast from London urging the French to keep fighting
The armistice France signed with Germany after its defeat that June
questions.explanation: Speaking on the BBC from London, de Gaulle rejected the coming armistice and called on the French to keep up the fight. It is seen as the start of the Free French movement.

questions.stem: Why is the national anthem called « La Marseillaise »?
options: Napoléon chose it after a victory near Marseille in 1796.
Volunteers from Marseille sang it as they marched to Paris in 1792.
It was composed in Marseille by a local choirmaster in 1792.
It was first performed at the opening of Marseille's opera house.
questions.explanation: Rouget de Lisle wrote the song in Strasbourg in 1792. It took its name from volunteers from Marseille who sang it on their way to Paris. Saying it was composed in Marseille is the usual mistake.

questions.stem: Why does Villers-Bretonneux, in northern France, hold an Anzac Day service?
options: The Anzacs were formed there before going to Gallipoli.
Australia's first prime minister was born there.
Australian troops recaptured the town in April 1918.
Australian troops first landed in France there in 1915.
questions.explanation: Australian forces retook the town on 24–25 April 1918, and the town keeps strong links with Australia. The Australian National Memorial stands nearby. Gallipoli, in Türkiye, is where the Anzac landing took place.

questions.stem: Géographe Bay and Cape Naturaliste in Western Australia are named after what?
options: The ships of the French Baudin expedition
Two French scientists who settled in Perth
The ships of La Pérouse's expedition to Botany Bay
French words for the region's landscapes
questions.explanation: Nicolas Baudin's expedition of 1801–1803 charted much of Australia's southern and western coast in « le Géographe » and « le Naturaliste ». La Pérouse's ships were « la Boussole » and « l'Astrolabe ».

questions.stem: The Sydney suburb of La Perouse is named after whom?
options: A French governor of New South Wales in the 1800s
A French navigator who reached Botany Bay in 1788
A French convict transported on the First Fleet
A French priest who founded a school in Sydney
questions.explanation: Lapérouse's expedition arrived at Botany Bay in January 1788, just days after the First Fleet. It sailed on and was lost in the Pacific. New South Wales never had a French governor.

questions.stem: What is hidden in a « galette des rois »?
questions.explanation: The galette is eaten for Epiphany in January, and whoever finds the « fève » becomes king or queen for the day. « La bûche » is the Christmas log cake.

questions.stem: In Provence, what are « les santons »?
options: Small clay figures for Christmas nativity scenes
Bunches of dried herbs hung in kitchens
Bells that ring to announce Easter
Fields of lavender grown for perfume
questions.explanation: Santons are traditional painted figures, from the holy family to village bakers, set out in the Christmas crib. They are a well-known craft of Provence.

questions.stem: What do people traditionally eat at « la Chandeleur », on 2 February?
questions.explanation: La Chandeleur is celebrated with crêpes, and some flip them holding a coin for luck. The galette des rois belongs to Epiphany, a month earlier.

questions.stem: What is traditionally given on 1 May in France?
options: A sprig of lily of the valley
A box of chocolate Easter eggs
questions.explanation: On 1 May, the Fête du Travail, people give « du muguet » (lily of the valley) for luck, and street sellers offer it. Chocolate eggs belong to Easter.

questions.stem: Which regional language is spoken in Brittany?
questions.explanation: Breton is a Celtic language, related to Welsh. Basque is spoken in the south-west, occitan across the south, and alsacien in the east.

questions.stem: Which dish is associated with Marseille?
questions.explanation: Bouillabaisse is a Provençal fish stew from the port of Marseille. Choucroute comes from Alsace and tartiflette from Savoie.

questions.stem: In mainland France, when are « les grandes vacances »?
questions.explanation: The long summer holiday falls in the northern summer, and the school year starts again at « la rentrée » in September. An Australian student would expect December and January.

questions.stem: Who held one of the first public paid film screenings, in Paris in 1895?
questions.explanation: Auguste and Louis Lumière screened short films with their cinématographe in December 1895. Méliès, inspired by them, went on to pioneer special effects.

questions.stem: What is the top prize at the Cannes Film Festival?
questions.explanation: The Palme d'or is awarded at Cannes each May. The Césars are France's national film awards, and the Golden Lion and Golden Bear are given in Venice and Berlin.

questions.stem: Which architectural style is the cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris?
questions.explanation: Notre-Dame, begun in the 12th century, is a landmark of Gothic architecture, with flying buttresses and rose windows. Romanesque, the style before Gothic, has thick walls and round arches.

questions.stem: For what event was the Eiffel Tower built?
options: The end of the First World War
questions.explanation: The tower was the entrance arch to the 1889 world's fair, which also marked a century since the Revolution. It was meant to be temporary.

questions.stem: Which painting gave Impressionism its name?
options: Renoir's « Bal du moulin de la Galette »
questions.explanation: A critic mocked Monet's painting of the port of Le Havre, and the name of the movement stuck. Manet is often linked with the Impressionists, but he did not exhibit with them.

questions.stem: Why is French called « la langue de Molière »?
options: After Molière, who founded the Académie française
After Molière, the great 17th-century writer of comic plays
After Molière, who wrote the first French dictionary
After Molière, a king who made French the official language
questions.explanation: Molière wrote comedies such as « Le Malade imaginaire » and is seen as the model of the language, as Shakespeare is for English. The Académie was founded by Cardinal Richelieu.

questions.stem: Who wrote « Les Misérables »?
questions.explanation: Victor Hugo published « Les Misérables » in 1862, and also wrote « Notre-Dame de Paris ». Saint-Exupéry wrote « Le Petit Prince ».

questions.stem: When is « la Fête de la musique » held each year?
questions.explanation: Started in 1982, it falls on the summer solstice, when musicians of every level play free in the streets. It is now held in many countries.

questions.stem: What is the difference between « la haute couture » and « le prêt-à-porter »?
options: Ready-to-wear clothing, and made-to-measure luxury fashion
Fashion shown in Paris, and fashion shown abroad
Made-to-measure luxury fashion, and ready-to-wear clothing
questions.explanation: Haute couture is hand-made to measure by a small number of recognised Paris houses. Prêt-à-porter is produced in standard sizes. Reversing the two is the common mistake.

questions.stem: You are writing a brochure for younger students about la Chandeleur. Which features suit this text type?
options: Questions and answers set out as a script for two speakers
Headings, short sections and exclamations to engage readers
A formal greeting and a closing formula with « veuillez agréer »
A date and place at the top and « Cher journal » to open
questions.explanation: A brochure informs and engages, so it uses headings, short sections and lively features such as exclamations. The formal closing belongs to a letter, and « cher journal » to a journal entry.
